high_pressure_washing.secondary_impacts: High disturbance; drives oil down if used on soft substrate

low_pressure_flushing.secondary_impacts: Can drive oil into sediment if misapplied; mobilised oil must be recovered

low_pressure_heated_flushing.secondary_impacts: Heat harms sensitive biota; excluded on wetlands

manual_removal.secondary_impacts: Trampling and foot traffic can damage soft sediment and vegetation

mechanical_removal.secondary_impacts: Sediment loss and habitat damage; excluded on marsh and mudflat

natural_attenuation.secondary_impacts: Oil persists longer where energy is low; monitoring effort only

passive_sorbents.secondary_impacts: Sorbent waste generation; limited to mobile oil

sediment_mixing.secondary_impacts: Can bury or spread oil; not for soft or sensitive habitat

sediment_relocation.secondary_impacts: Redistributes oil; only on exposed beaches

solidifiers.secondary_impacts: Added material and waste; limited field evidence

surface_washing_agents.secondary_impacts: Chemical residue and mobilised-oil recovery concerns

vacuum_removal.secondary_impacts: Access and equipment disturbance; removes free oil only

vegetation_cutting.secondary_impacts: Removes biomass and can increase erosion; only where sensitivity is high

inputs.class_rules: E excluded > A benefit > D harm under conditions > B no clear evidence; C natural recovery
inputs.ordering: within a class: lower bound of the 90% benefit interval where it exists (edge loss avoided by year 8 in m, then vegetation cover ratio at year 2, then literature lnRR lower bound; units are never mixed), then the ASSUMED ecological score (higher = lower disturbance first), then name

category_rules.conditional: class D (allowed, harm flagged under some conditions or mixed evidence), OR class A when the input is outside the scope where the benefit evidence was gathered (transfer untested), OR class A when the option presupposes a method that is itself excluded
category_rules.excluded: class E: removed by a hard constraint (screening rule or habitat rating) or by evidence of harm
category_rules.insufficient_evidence: class B with no eligible evidence rows: no comparison with natural recovery is possible
category_rules.natural_recovery_monitoring: class C: natural recovery, the reference every option is compared with
category_rules.no_demonstrated_benefit: class B with evidence rows that show no clear difference from natural recovery
category_rules.recommended: class A (evidence of benefit, no harm flag) AND the input is inside the scope where that evidence was gathered (scope tier 'validated')
